question: The Milky Way should hold something like 100 million black holes the mass of stars. Why have only a few dozen been found?
options: Most are alone and give off nothing
answer: Most are alone and give off nothing. Nearly every known one was found because it is stripping gas from a partner star, and that gas glows in X-rays as it falls. A black hole with no partner has nothing to heat, so it sits dark among the stars.
move: A list of finds shows what is easy to see, not what is there.
ask: Which quiet people around me do I overlook simply because they never make any noise?
trap: Dust, because it already hides so much of the galaxy from view.
reference: Corral-Santana et al., BlackCAT: A catalogue of stellar-mass black holes in X-ray transients, Astronomy & Astrophysics, 2016
